issues.description: All 11 exact catalog-listed table probes succeeded and returned the requested column names, but each read one row with coverage_verified=false. Required history includes Compustat annual/quarterly comparability records for 1995–2022 and the 15-quarter lookback with 14–16 complete records, plus the 1999–2022 event construction, CRSP daily two-quarter buffers (1 Jul 1998–30 Jun 2023), linked quarterly/monthly observations and I/B/E/S fiscal-period/report-date matches. Probe samples do not establish the required rows, identifiers or full history.

The catalog describes CRSP.DSIX as a capitalization-decile series while the author program uses its VWRETD field as the market return; the candidate's exact series meaning remains unverified. COMP.COMPANY exposes the probed GICS classification field names, but its GVKEY population and field coding are not established. The source joins these classifications by GVKEY without date matching, so no time-varying historical-classification panel is required.

The sample builder includes WRDS CIBESLINK and ICLINK source files under [redacted-path-4a3670aff8a2] and reads the resulting CIBESLNK/Home.ICLINK link inputs inside a remote-submit workflow. Those include files, remote SAS/CONNECT configuration and the generated link table's complete schema/population were not verified; no access or entitlement barrier is inferred.

Stata requires data/eco 97-24.xls, sheet 5424185_20240104_214940_eco, and imported Event, DateTime and B variables for the 1997–2022 event filters. The workbook is not in the frozen package inventory; the datasheet names Bloomberg Terminal as the source, but a compatible local workbook, sheet/column mapping and access route were not verified.

The Stata script consumes naicsh10, gind10, sich5 and sich3 panels in addition to the sich10 baseline. The supplied SAS producer supports the industry/day-gap macro settings, but its recorded default is only sich/10; the four additional outputs must be generated with consistent settings at both producer assignments before Stata consumes them.

The SAS master, preparation/companion files and Stata entry point contain author-host Windows project roots. A writable, host-visible working copy with the same code/data/log directory relationships must be configured before a later attempt; this is path setup, not a scientific source repair.

The supplied Stata analysis invokes winsor2 and eststo. The exact-name eststo command check succeeded; winsor2 was not found in the two adopaths checked by the original environment probe, and availability outside those paths remains unverified.

The original environment probe did not establish successful SAS startup. The supplied workflow requires SAS remote-submit, PROC CAS for master logging, PROC REG/SURVEYSELECT, PROC EXPAND, and DBMS=STATA/EXCEL export support. Runtime/product/service availability remains unverified; the recorded startup diagnostic is not evidence of a license barrier.

evidence.quote:
proc sql;
		create table announce_ibes(drop=usfirm fdate ldate score) as
		select distinct *, count(distinct fqtr) as nqtr "Number of Announcements" 
		from cibeslnk as a left join (select distinct ticker, pends, measure, pdicity, anndats, anntims, value as actual, usfirm,
											 year(pends) as fyear, qtr(pends) as fqtr 
							from ibes.actu_epsus where measure='EPS' and pdicity='QTR' and usfirm=1 
							and not missing(anndats) and not missing(anntims)and anndats>=pends
							and &begdate<=pends<=&enddate) as b
		on a.ticker=b.ticker 
		group by permno, fyear
		order by gvkey, permno, fyear;

		create table announce_ibes(drop=mintime) as
		select distinct *, min(anntims) as mintime
		from announce_ibes
		group by permno, anndats
		having calculated mintime=anntims;
	quit;

create table EAD2 as 
		select distinct a.*, b.permno as permno_p
		from EAD1 as a, EAD as b
		where a.&industry=b.&industry and a.fyear=b.fyear and a.fqtr=b.fqtr and a.permno_f ne b.permno
		and b.EAD>a.EAD1 and b.EAD-a.EAD1>=&daysapart /*using ten/five/three days between focal and peer EADs*/
		order by &industry, fyear, fqtr, EAD1, permno_f, permno_p;

		create table EAD2 as 
		select distinct *, count(permno_p) as npeers
		from EAD2

		order by &industry, fyear, fqtr, EAD1, permno_f, permno_p;
